clue.text: Fighter crew here, then and now

definitions.text: Fighter crew here, then and now

parts.words: Fighter crew here, then and now
parts.note: in the past the fighters were gamecocks crowing in a pit for cockfighting; today the fighter is a warplane whose crew sits in the pilot's compartment

explanation.surface: A question about where the crew of a fighter plane has always sat.
explanation.walkthrough: The word once meant the pit where cocks fought, and now means the pilot's compartment of a plane, so both 'then and now' a fighter's crew is there.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names the cockfighting arena of old and the pilot's compartment of a modern aircraft.

clue.text: Author's cloak

definitions.meaning: Truman ..., the American writer of In Cold Blood; the 's stands for 'is'
a long hooded cloak or mantle worn by soldiers and travellers

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the surname of the American novelist Truman; the other is a long hooded cloak.

clue.text: Finding ring hidden in cropped grain needs some brains

indicators.note: the ring is tucked away inside the shortened grain word, so one piece goes within the other
a cropped word has its tail cut off, here the final letter of the grain

parts.note: cereal is grain such as wheat or oats
to ring is to sound a bell; a bell gives a ring

explanation.surface: A farmer finds a ring in the stubble of a harvested field, which takes some intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finding' and 'needs' are link words; 'cropped' trims the grain and 'hidden in' tucks the ring inside, so the A of the grain ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebella is the plural of cerebellum, the part of the brain at the back of the skull, so several are some brains.

clue.text: Playwright taught us rhyme

parts.note: a Roman comic dramatist whose name rhymes with the phrase taught us, as a schoolroom memory aid might put it

explanation.surface: A dramatist once gave us lessons in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rhyme' tells you the playwright's name rhymes with 'taught us'; the surface wants it to mean a playwright taught us how to rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman comic playwright of the third century BC whose comedies inspired Shakespeare's Comedy of Errors.

clue.text: Economist joins tramp in hard labour

parts.note: to tramp is to tread heavily
John Stuart Mill, the nineteenth-century political economist

explanation.surface: An economist teams up with a vagrant in a prison work gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tramp' looks like a vagrant but is the verb, to tread; Mill is the English economist and philosopher J.S. Mill.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill was a wheel turned by prisoners' feet as a punishment, and figuratively means monotonous toil.

clue.text: Convert from unreliable electricity — it's twice been cut off

indicators.note: unreliable means not to be trusted to stay as it is, so the letters are rearranged
the letters of the pair are removed from the electricity word before the shuffle
the pair is taken two times over

parts.note: the word it, with the 's meaning 'is' and adding no letters

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the power supply is unreliable because it has been cut off twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' and 'been cut off' strip two copies of IT from ELECTRICITY, leaving ELECRCY; 'unreliable' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To recycle waste is to convert it into reusable material.

clue.text: Privileges announced in formal procedure

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word for privileges is said rather than spelt

parts.note: rights are privileges or entitlements

explanation.surface: Special entitlements are declared as part of a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Rites are the set forms of a religious or solemn ceremony, a formal procedure.

clue.text: Horse finds old way in to a Moorish city

indicators.note: the old way is placed in the horse word, splitting it after its first letter

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
the letter A, joined on to the end; 'to' means added to

explanation.surface: A rider's horse follows an ancient track into a city of Moorish Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Córdoba in Andalusia was the capital of the Moorish caliphate and is famous for its Great Mosque.

clue.text: Palm a drink

parts.note: the coco is the coconut palm

explanation.surface: Someone palms off a drink, or a palm tree yields a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot drink made from the ground seeds of the cacao tree.

clue.text: Beverage gives energy, thus absorbing iron

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the iron goes inside the word for thus

parts.note: so means thus, in that way
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: A drink gives a boost, and so contains iron, like a health claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iron' suggests the metal Fe, but here it is the verb, to press clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong black coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans, a beverage.

clue.text: About-to follow forecaster's system that's not changing

indicators.note: to follow means to come after, so the word for about is placed after the system

parts.note: in British football pools, a perm (short for permutation) is a punter's system for forecasting results
anent is an old word meaning about or concerning

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster's system is about to be adopted permanently.
explanation.walkthrough: The FOOTBALL POOLS are a British betting game on match results. The forecaster looks like a weatherman, but here is a pools punter forecasting scores, and 'About' is ANENT, meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something permanent lasts for ever without changing.

clue.text: MP, losing note, is to go over chief points again

indicators.note: losing means giving up, so the note is taken out of the military policeman

parts.note: a redcap is a British military policeman, named for the red cap cover
D is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A Member of Parliament loses a vote and must go back over the main arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: MP looks like a Member of Parliament but means military police; dropping D from REDCAP leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to recapitulate, restating the main points of what has been said.

clue.text: Closed part in apocryphal book

parts.note: a door pushed to is closed
a bit is a part or piece

explanation.surface: Something shut away inside a book outside the accepted canon.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobit is a book of the Apocrypha telling of a pious Jew blinded and cured with the help of an angel.

clue.text: Put out animal caught by oldies misbehaving

indicators.note: caught by means trapped inside, so the animal sits within the rearranged elderly people
misbehaving means acting out of order, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: A pet is grabbed by unruly pensioners, who get it shut outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' gives DISLOE, the anagram of the oldies, and 'caught by' sets the animal inside it; 'Put out' reads as extinguish but means displace a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: To put out a joint, such as a shoulder, is to dislocate it.

clue.text: Skinflint's smart to get into smaller show

indicators.note: to get into means to enter, so the pieces go inside the word for smaller

parts.note: less means smaller in amount
a miser is a skinflint; the 's is the link 'is', adding no letters
able means clever or smart

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted person is sharp enough to get into a cheaper show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinflint's smart' reads as a stingy man being clever; in fact the two words supply separate pieces, the 's being a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Les Misérables is a long-running stage musical, a show based on Victor Hugo's novel.

clue.text: Is being embraced by former partner really delightful?

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: being embraced by means held inside, so the little word sits within the word for really

parts.note: quite means really or truly
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about whether a hug from an old flame is truly lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: Exquisite means extremely beautiful or delicate, so delightful in a refined way.

clue.text: Brood over wine store —- it holds nothing of value

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means on top of, so the brood comes before the store

parts.note: a litter is a brood of young animals born together
a bin is a rack or store for bottles of wine

explanation.surface: A nesting bird broods above a wine cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brood' looks like a verb (to worry) but is the noun, a litter of young.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubbish receptacle holds only refuse, things thrown away as worthless.

clue.text: Cover for food that's broken in the hatch

definitions.text: Cover for food that's broken in the hatch

parts.words: Cover for food that's broken in the hatch
parts.note: the protective casing of something to eat, which is cracked open when a chick hatches out; the surface suggests a cover in a serving hatch

explanation.surface: A lid for a dish has been smashed in the kitchen serving hatch.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'hatch' looks like the serving hatch between kitchen and dining room, but it is the chick hatching out.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin brittle shell of an egg covers the food inside and is broken when the chick hatches.

clue.text: Self-important organ lent quid unwisely

indicators.note: unwisely means done foolishly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lends a pound to a church organ fund without thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unwisely' rearranges ORGAN, LENT and QUID together.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandiloquent means pompous or bombastic in style, as a self-important speaker is.

clue.text: Muscle is slow to react when the yen isn't there

indicators.note: isn't there means absent, so the letter for the yen is removed from the word for slow

parts.note: dilatory means tardy or slow to act
Y is the abbreviation for the yen, Japan's currency

explanation.surface: A muscle is sluggish to respond when the desire for action is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' looks like a longing; it is the Japanese currency, Y, and 'isn't there' takes it from DILATORY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilator is a muscle that widens an opening of the body, such as the pupil.

clue.text: Mistake of traitor trapped by signs of hesitation

indicators.note: trapped by means caught inside, so the traitor goes within the hesitation sounds

parts.note: er and um are sounds made when hesitating
a rat is a traitor or informer

explanation.surface: A turncoat is caught out by his hesitant ums and ers, giving away his error.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in print, a mistake listed for correction.

clue.text: Death on stage? Story shows the opposite

indicators.note: the opposite of death on stage means the order is flipped, so the stage piece comes first

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
end means death

explanation.surface: A theatre critic finds a dying scene shows the reverse of the tale.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' would set death above the stage; 'shows the opposite' flips that order, and 'Death on stage' falsely suggests a theatrical dying scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional story, often about heroic deeds.

clue.text: Mark bar structure left by church composer

parts.note: a scar is a mark on the skin

indicators.note: left by means abandoned by, so the church letters are dropped from the structure

parts.note: a lattice is a structure of crossed bars
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A scratch on a structure of bars left by someone at church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left by' drops CE from LATTICE, leaving LATTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Domenico Scarlatti was an Italian baroque composer famous for his keyboard sonatas.

clue.text: Traveller finding a nice cove

parts.note: a gent is a refined man; cove is old slang for a man

explanation.surface: A traveller comes upon a pleasant little bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cove' looks like a bay; it is old slang for a man, and 'nice' suggests a gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial traveller is a sales agent who travels to sell goods.

clue.text: Simple putt, thanks to the flag

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
in golf, the pin is the flagstick in the hole

explanation.surface: A golfer sinks an easy putt thanks to the flagstick.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap-in is a very short putt that only needs a light tap into the hole.

clue.text: Engineers have day before magistrate

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers of the British Army
an eve is the day before a festival

explanation.surface: Army engineers get a day off ahead of seeing a magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local chief magistrate or official in medieval England.

clue.text: Upright installed in Brontë rectory

indicators.note: installed in means set within, so the letters lie inside the run of words

explanation.surface: An upright piece of furniture was placed in the Haworth parsonage of the Brontës.
explanation.walkthrough: The run across 'Brontë rectory' (the ë standing for plain E) gives the answer; the Brontë sisters lived at Haworth rectory.
explanation.definitionFit: Erect means standing straight up, an adjective for upright.

clue.text: Slot machine's about right fit for Times

indicators.note: about means around, so the slot machine goes round the letter for right

parts.note: a pin table is a pinball machine; the 's is a link 'is'

explanation.surface: A newspaper reviews whether a fruit machine is suitable for its pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts PINTABLE around R, after P.
explanation.definitionFit: Printable means decent enough to be published in a newspaper such as The Times.

clue.text: Recently was in charge of papal church

parts.note: late means recently, as in of late
ran means managed or was in charge

explanation.surface: A papal church recently had someone in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: St John Lateran in Rome is the Pope's cathedral, the papal church.

clue.text: Three leaders leaving with resolution come to like the Lords

indicators.note: the first three letters, the leaders, depart from the start of the word

parts.note: determined means having resolution

explanation.surface: Three leaders walk out resolutely and come to look like peers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three leaders leaving' removes DET from DETERMINED. The House of Lords is Britain's upper chamber, whose peers wear ermine-trimmed robes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermined means trimmed with ermine fur, as the ceremonial robes of peers are.
